hook: A submarine volcanic eruption created 50 hectares of land off Japan.

sections.voiceover: A submarine volcanic eruption created 50 hectares of land off Japan.

sections.voiceover: On October 27, an underwater volcanic eruption began off Ioto. The Japan Coast Guard confirmed an underwater volcanic eruption off Ioto created new land. Where did this 125-acre expansion stretch off Iwo Jima?
sections.visual_cue: Map graphic zooming into Ioto in the Ogasawara Islands while Coast Guard vessel monitors smoking coastline.
sections.sfx_cue: Radar sweep with ocean surf sound
b_roll: Japan Coast Guard patrol vessel off Ioto shore
Topographic mapping line expanding along Iwo Jima coastline

sections.voiceover: However, NASA's Earth Observatory confirmed it's attached directly to the existing black sand beach.
sections.visual_cue: NASA Earth Observatory split screen showing black sand beach baseline before and after new land mass joined.
b_roll: NASA Earth Observatory satellite imagery comparison
Close drone pass over fresh black volcanic sand shore
sections.animation_cue: Split-screen slider transition showing terrain growth

sections.voiceover: NASA's Earth Observatory reported that the submarine eruption added 50 hectares of land. Seoul Economic Daily noted the total area equals 10 Tokyo Domes.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic scale line measuring distance from Tokyo to Iwo Jima, morphing into 10 stadium footprint outlines over the beach.
b_roll: Graphic distance scale from Tokyo south into Pacific Ocean
Architectural aerial footage of Tokyo Dome stadium for scale
sections.animation_cue: 3D stadium outlines multiplying across new terrain map

sections.voiceover: 50 hectares of new land created by submarine volcanic fire.
sections.visual_cue: Wide drone camera shot panning across fresh smoking black sand beach meeting open Pacific waves.
b_roll: Sweeping drone view of new volcanic coastline
Steaming Pacific shoreline against fresh black sand
